description: An offset scale is padded by its own two entries in `config.scale`, and by a constant that is not an entry at all. Upstream sends the offset channels down a second arm of each rule: `} else if (isXorYOffset(channel)) { if (scaleType === ScaleType.BAND) return scaleConfig.offsetBandPaddingInner; }` for the inner padding, and `} else if (isXorYOffset(channel)) { if (scaleType === ScaleType.POINT) { return 0.5; } else if (scaleType === ScaleType.BAND) return scaleConfig.offsetBandPaddingOuter; }` for the outer. This compiler had neither arm. `offsetBandPaddingInner` and `offsetBandPaddingOuter` were never read, and because they have no default the omission was silent until a theme wrote one; and the point case read `pointPadding`, which agreed only by the accident that its default is the same 0.5 the comment calls for — the half-step that puts an offset point on the centre of the band a bar would have filled. The first row is a grouped bar, where the inner scale takes the theme's 0.3 and 0.15 while the outer band keeps the wider nested-offset padding that separates the groups. The second row offsets points down the other axis — a second channel rather than the same one, because a concatenation shares an offset scale across its views and the two would otherwise be merged into one — and its outer padding must stay 0.5 even though the theme has narrowed every point scale to 0.2, since that number is a constant and not the configured one. The third row is a point scale with no offset at all, where `pointPadding` does apply and must read 0.2, so the two are told apart rather than assumed alike.
